description: Religious longing and facts merely compatible with Christianity provide no support unless a demonstrable link connects Christianity’s explanation to the experiences or facts invoked.
critique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty directly answers Knechtle’s appeal to hope and religious fulfillment by distinguishing observations consistent with Christianity from evidence that specifically connects those observations to Christianity’s explanatory account. Principal limitation: His claim that non-falsifiability makes evidence impossible overstates the methodological point, while assertions that human invention explains every religion and Christianity has zero support receive no defense here. Live burden: The reply needs an articulated account of what evidential connection would discriminate Christianity from natural explanations, especially if Knechtle argues cumulative experiential fit supplies probabilistic rather than demonstrative support. Locked score: 80 appropriately reflects exceptional reply contact and burden relevance alongside a coherent compatibility-versus-evidence distinction, while reserving credit for the move’s unsupported universality, compressed epistemology, and insufficiently charitable scope.
